# Causality

> A mathematical programme and learning architectures for systems that can change their descriptions and organisation.



- [About Causality](https://causality.in/about/index.md): How Causality connects changing descriptions, learning within a unit and learning among units, with experiments that test what helps. ([HTML](https://causality.in/about/))

- [Beyond the Mirage: a framework for AGI classification and controllable progress](https://causality.in/blog/beyond-the-mirage/index.md): The proposed Agentic Causal Intelligence framework separates causal reasoning from autonomy, then asks what evidence and controls each capability needs. ([HTML](https://causality.in/blog/beyond-the-mirage/))

- [Entropy and a learning mind](https://causality.in/blog/entropy-and-a-learning-mind/index.md): A broken mug starts an early question about neural networks: what happens to useful initial intuitions when learning never stops? ([HTML](https://causality.in/blog/entropy-and-a-learning-mind/))

- [The future can constrain a model without sending a message back](https://causality.in/blog/future-without-retrocausation/index.md): An endpoint calculation asks how a future condition shapes a whole path, and where its information enters the problem. ([HTML](https://causality.in/blog/future-without-retrocausation/))

- [Blog](https://causality.in/blog/index.md): Worked questions about distinctions, causal evidence and learning under limits. ([HTML](https://causality.in/blog/))

- [The ineffable geometry](https://causality.in/blog/the-ineffable-geometry/index.md): A vocabulary we do not yet share, a line through an imagined time, and an early hunch about geometry, causality and intelligence. ([HTML](https://causality.in/blog/the-ineffable-geometry/))

- [The record and the arrow](https://causality.in/blog/the-record-and-the-arrow/index.md): A reversible motion leaves an ambiguous record: where did the recoverable past disappear? ([HTML](https://causality.in/blog/the-record-and-the-arrow/))

- [When effects cancel along a path](https://causality.in/blog/when-effects-cancel/index.md): An exact xor model makes two interventions compose differently, leaving a path without the expected end-to-end effect. ([HTML](https://causality.in/blog/when-effects-cancel/))

- [When the support moves](https://causality.in/blog/when-the-support-moves/index.md): A measurement beyond the old endpoint changes what one sample can establish; an exact test follows the consequence. ([HTML](https://causality.in/blog/when-the-support-moves/))

- [What can you distinguish with one more move?](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/from-summary-to-repair/budgeted-questions/index.md): Rotating three bits makes another feature visible and spends part of the observer's remaining investigation. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/from-summary-to-repair/budgeted-questions/))

- [Compression is a promise about questions](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/from-summary-to-repair/compression-is-a-promise/index.md): Yesterday's summary answered every question we asked. A new question reveals the distinction it chose not to keep. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/from-summary-to-repair/compression-is-a-promise/))

- [From summary to repair](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/from-summary-to-repair/index.md): An ordered path from a lost answer through affordable questions to the full cost of an accessible repair. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/from-summary-to-repair/))

- [The price of another question](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/from-summary-to-repair/the-price-of-another-question/index.md): A finite query tree finds the cheapest complete repair, rather than the cheapest first read. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/from-summary-to-repair/the-price-of-another-question/))

- [Changing descriptions](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/index.md): What survives a changed question, a noisy observation or another representational basis? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/))

- [How tolerances accumulate](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/preservation-under-uncertainty/how-tolerances-accumulate/index.md): Each replacement stays close to its predecessor. How far can the chain travel from the original? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/preservation-under-uncertainty/how-tolerances-accumulate/))

- [Preservation under uncertainty](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/preservation-under-uncertainty/index.md): What remains usable when observations are noisy, experiments are simulated and approximations accumulate? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/preservation-under-uncertainty/))

- [When one experiment can stand in for another](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/preservation-under-uncertainty/one-experiment-through-another/index.md): A common simulator transfers a decision rule between observation laws. Its error controls the change in bounded loss. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/preservation-under-uncertainty/one-experiment-through-another/))

- [A noisy answer is not an exact repair](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/preservation-under-uncertainty/recovering-a-distinction-from-a-noisy-answer/index.md): A one-bit report can be useful without restoring the missing bit. Repetition changes risk only when it supplies new evidence. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/preservation-under-uncertainty/recovering-a-distinction-from-a-noisy-answer/))

- [When the description must change](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/when-the-description-must-change/index.md): A perfect estimate cannot supply a relation its language never represented. What would make that inadequacy visible? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/when-the-description-must-change/))

- [Which factors did we recover?](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/which-factors-did-we-recover/index.md): Independent latent coordinates and perfect reconstruction need not identify the quantities we intended to describe. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/changing-descriptions/which-factors-did-we-recover/))

- [Change the rule without moving the finish line](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/changing-the-rule/index.md): What happens when an evolving routing rule can improve its score by changing what counts as success? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/changing-the-rule/))

- [What would count as emergent hierarchy?](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/from-unit-to-swarm/emergence-needs-a-comparison/index.md): An early cue and a later request reach different units. Can their learned organisation carry the relation into an answer? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/from-unit-to-swarm/emergence-needs-a-comparison/))

- [From unit to swarm](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/from-unit-to-swarm/index.md): Compare a unit's contract, a composition's joint constraints and the contribution of its organisation. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/from-unit-to-swarm/))

- [Three tests for a reasoning unit](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/from-unit-to-swarm/three-tests-for-a-reasoning-unit/index.md): A replacement model returns a valid reply but fails the caller's task; the shared boundary gives three different things to investigate. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/from-unit-to-swarm/three-tests-for-a-reasoning-unit/))

- [Every pair can agree while the whole differs](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/from-unit-to-swarm/when-pairs-agree-and-the-whole-differs/index.md): Matching pairs can leave incompatible wholes possible; parity and simultaneous reservations reveal different missing relations. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/from-unit-to-swarm/when-pairs-agree-and-the-whole-differs/))

- [Composition and learning](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/index.md): What can reasoning units learn through their organisation, and how can we distinguish that contribution from the abilities of their parts? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/))

- [Comparing a quantum unit with its classical counterpart](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/quantum-comparison/index.md): Where does a quantum candidate's useful contribution survive preparation, measurement and comparison with classical methods? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/quantum-comparison/))

- [Recovery across a changing world](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/recovery-across-a-changing-world/index.md): A saved swarm returns to a world whose leases and components have changed; what can its recovery actually preserve? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/recovery-across-a-changing-world/))

- [What should a surprise change?](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/what-should-a-surprise-change/index.md): A traffic prediction fails. Should the unit remember the event, adjust a parameter or propose another account of the road? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/composition-and-learning/what-should-a-surprise-change/))

- [Did the cache make it faster?](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/causal-inference-primer/index.md): Latency falls after a cache rollout. Which comparison could separate the cache's contribution from the changing traffic? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/causal-inference-primer/))

- [EMA and Bayesian updates for online scoring](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/ema-vs-bayesian-updates/index.md): Follow an implemented EMA update into delayed-cue retention, then compare what a candidate Bayesian estimate would add. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/ema-vs-bayesian-updates/))

- [Four questions behind a benchmark result](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/four-questions-for-an-evaluation/index.md): A retention policy beats learned utility and loses to no memory: four questions examine what the completed benchmark supports. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/four-questions-for-an-evaluation/))

- [From observation to evaluation](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/index.md): Follow an engineering intervention into the question of how a memory score earns trust. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/))

- [What did selective memory buy?](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/what-did-selective-memory-buy/index.md): Reckon's completed memory experiments find small gains, a loss against no memory, and a large price for measuring which records to retain. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/from-observation-to-evaluation/what-did-selective-memory-buy/))

- [What does the measurement establish?](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/index.md): A record gets its chance to be useful through the policy that selects it. How can its contribution be estimated? ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/evidence-and-evaluation/))

- [Thoughts](https://causality.in/collections/index.md): Three connected inquiries: what a summary preserves, what units learn through how they are organised and what an evaluation shows about a change. Each begins with a question and develops it through small examples; standalone pieces are on the Blog. ([HTML](https://causality.in/collections/))

- [Why communication and memory are computation](https://causality.in/hena/communication-and-memory/index.md): Follow how local views, sparse messages and limited collective memory could contribute to HENA’s answer. ([HTML](https://causality.in/hena/communication-and-memory/))

- [How units form a collective](https://causality.in/hena/how-units-form-a-collective/index.md): Follow a repair example to see how local reasoning, a few messages and limited memory could help units solve a task together. ([HTML](https://causality.in/hena/how-units-form-a-collective/))

- [HENA](https://causality.in/hena/index.md): A research project on how small reasoning units learn to solve a task together, the collective that the Causality programme works towards. ([HTML](https://causality.in/hena/))

- [HENA mentions](https://causality.in/hena/mentions/index.md): Writing that discusses or references HENA across the connected publications. ([HTML](https://causality.in/hena/mentions/))

- [Some questions need another description.](https://causality.in/index.md): A mathematical programme and learning architectures for systems that can change their descriptions and organisation. ([HTML](https://causality.in/))

- [Descriptions and repair](https://causality.in/monad/descriptions-and-repair/index.md): See which answers survive a shorter description and when a missing distinction needs a richer one. ([HTML](https://causality.in/monad/descriptions-and-repair/))

- [MONAD](https://causality.in/monad/index.md): A calculus for preserving, compressing and changing what a description can express. ([HTML](https://causality.in/monad/))

- [MONAD mentions](https://causality.in/monad/mentions/index.md): Writing that discusses or references MONAD across the connected publications. ([HTML](https://causality.in/monad/mentions/))

- [What a summary preserves](https://causality.in/monad/what-a-summary-preserves/index.md): Work through answer-preserving compression and the different ways a missing distinction can be repaired. ([HTML](https://causality.in/monad/what-a-summary-preserves/))

- [Computation, state and learning](https://causality.in/muon/computation-state-and-learning/index.md): Follow a road notice into the next route answer and see how MUON would compare different reasoning units. ([HTML](https://causality.in/muon/computation-state-and-learning/))

- [How experience can change a unit](https://causality.in/muon/how-experience-changes-a-unit/index.md): Follow a road notice through an immediate answer, later recall, learning and a proposed change to the unit. ([HTML](https://causality.in/muon/how-experience-changes-a-unit/))

- [MUON](https://causality.in/muon/index.md): Research into how a small reasoning unit uses past observations, learns and works with other units. ([HTML](https://causality.in/muon/))

- [MUON mentions](https://causality.in/muon/mentions/index.md): Writing that discusses or references MUON across the connected publications. ([HTML](https://causality.in/muon/mentions/))

- [Privacy notice](https://causality.in/privacy/index.md): Website hosting, email contact, reading preferences and external reading assistance for RTEPL's editorial publications. ([HTML](https://causality.in/privacy/))

- [Q-HENA](https://causality.in/q-hena/index.md): Research into how quantum units share work, communicate and recover together. ([HTML](https://causality.in/q-hena/))

- [Q-HENA mentions](https://causality.in/q-hena/mentions/index.md): Writing that discusses or references Q-HENA across the connected publications. ([HTML](https://causality.in/q-hena/mentions/))

- [Quantum collective computation](https://causality.in/q-hena/quantum-collective-computation/index.md): Follow a proposed joint operation between two quantum units and see what changes when one must restart. ([HTML](https://causality.in/q-hena/quantum-collective-computation/))

- [Q-MUON](https://causality.in/q-muon/index.md): Research into a quantum reasoning unit that keeps MUON’s caller interface. ([HTML](https://causality.in/q-muon/))

- [Q-MUON mentions](https://causality.in/q-muon/mentions/index.md): Writing that discusses or references Q-MUON across the connected publications. ([HTML](https://causality.in/q-muon/mentions/))

- [The quantum local unit](https://causality.in/q-muon/the-quantum-local-unit/index.md): Follow a proposed quantum similarity calculation and see what a comparison with a classical unit would need to measure. ([HTML](https://causality.in/q-muon/the-quantum-local-unit/))

- [Cases, evaluations and decisions](https://causality.in/reckon/cases-evaluations-and-decisions/index.md): Follow two teams comparing a memory rule, from a shared test case to deciding whether to use it. ([HTML](https://causality.in/reckon/cases-evaluations-and-decisions/))

- [Compare two replay budgets](https://causality.in/reckon/compare-replay-budgets/index.md): Follow a local continual-classification comparison from matched inputs through saved accuracy matrices and event logs to their interpretation. ([HTML](https://causality.in/reckon/compare-replay-budgets/))

- [Reckon](https://causality.in/reckon/index.md): Measure what memory changes for its cost, and compare proposed improvements before deciding to use them. ([HTML](https://causality.in/reckon/))

- [Inspect an exported run](https://causality.in/reckon/inspect-an-exported-run/index.md): Follow a record through writes, reads and removals in a saved event log. ([HTML](https://causality.in/reckon/inspect-an-exported-run/))

- [Reckon mentions](https://causality.in/reckon/mentions/index.md): Writing that discusses or references Reckon across the connected publications. ([HTML](https://causality.in/reckon/mentions/))

- [Understand the memory laboratory](https://causality.in/reckon/understand-the-memory-laboratory/index.md): Choose a task, compare memory policies and read the saved results. ([HTML](https://causality.in/reckon/understand-the-memory-laboratory/))

- [Research projects](https://causality.in/research/index.md): The calculus, local units, collective architectures and measurement tools behind Causality’s research programme. ([HTML](https://causality.in/research/))
